scores.claim_text: FY25 revenue decline of $30.6M attributed in part to lower 'Army programs' volume (unnamed). Forward narrative still implies Army programs as material.
supports: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for 'Global Force Information Management' / 'GFIM' / contractor BigBear.ai — J-Book corpus does not cover the Army's services/IT line items where BBAI's Army work sits (corpus is hardware-heavy: MDA, Space Force, Air Force aircraft).

USAspending.query_dod_contracts(recipient='BigBear.ai') confirms only 6 DoD prime awards totaling $8.28M — including ONE Army GFIM follow-on production contract (W519TC24C0040, $3.9M). The Army GFIM follow-on is the primary identifiable Army program, but the filing does not name it.

USAspending(recipient='BigBear.ai Federal LLC') and (recipient='Pangiam') both return 0 awards — exact-string match fails. The $8.28M total via softer match strongly suggests BBAI's stated 'Army programs' are either (a) sub-tier work via prime contractors not visible in prime-award data, (b) IDIQ ceilings far exceeding obligated, or (c) a very small absolute base.
Filing self-discloses declining volume on Army programs — already an admission of weakening pipeline.
scores.M_value: NOT_FOUND in J-Book; USAspending confirms only $8.28M in prime DoD obligations total, of which $3.9M is a single Army GFIM follow-on production contract.
scores.interpretation: J-Book corpus coverage gap means pentagon_jbook cannot directly verify Army program funding trajectory. However, the cross-check via USAspending shows tiny prime-DoD obligations relative to FY25 revenue (~$128M) — strongly implying BBAI's Army revenue is sub-tier or IDIQ-ceiling-driven, with the company itself flagging declining volume. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: forward narrative leans on 'Army programs' that are not named and not visible at scale in prime-award data, while company admits volume is declining.

scores.claim_text: Ask Sage claimed as central pillar with 100,000 Department of War users; positioned as forward DoD generative AI revenue at scale.
supports: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for 'Ask Sage' / 'generative AI' / 'JADC2' — J-Book corpus does not include AI software platforms (likely buried in Operation & Maintenance or services PEs not in scope of the 410-PE corpus).

USAspending.query_dod_contracts(recipient='Ask Sage') confirms 42 awards totaling $23.07M, including a $10.88M task order with Army CIO G6 for the Ask Sage annual subscription/license/training. This is REAL but small relative to the $271.6M acquisition price BBAI paid.

The $23M of obligated DoD revenue across 42 awards is consistent with subscription/SaaS-style adoption but inconsistent with the implied 100,000 user / $271.6M acquisition valuation (~$2,700 per user) unless many users are unfunded pilots or free tiers.
scores.interpretation: Ask Sage has real DoD traction ($23M obligated, named Army CIO G6 customer) but the user-count claim implies revenue scale not supported by current obligations. $271.6M purchase price implies aggressive forward revenue multiple. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: real but materially smaller than narrative implies.

scores.claim_text: Customer concentration: $65M (51%) of FY25 revenue from >10%-customers; $27M of $248M backlog from same customers, expected 100% conversion by end-2026.
supports: Filing explicitly says contracts from significant customers 'are estimated to be completed during 2026' with ~100% expected to be recognized as revenue by end of 2026. This means 51% of current revenue is from customers whose remaining backlog ($27M) burns off during 2026 — implying a sharp forward revenue cliff if not replaced.

USAspending.query_dod_contracts(recipient='BigBear.ai') shows $8.28M total in prime DoD obligations; (recipient='BigBear.ai Federal LLC' exact) and (recipient='Pangiam') both return 0. The mismatch with reported $128M FY25 revenue indicates most revenue is via sub-tier or non-DoD channels — meaning the >10%-customer concentration is even more opaque and harder for outside investors to track or verify.
Filing does not name the >10% customers. Backlog burn-off + opaque customer ID + declining Army volume = concentrated forward cliff risk.
scores.M_value: BigBear.ai Federal LLC exact: 0 awards; BigBear.ai softer match: 6 awards / $8.28M; Pangiam: 0 awards
scores.interpretation: The combination of (a) 51% revenue from unnamed >10%-customers, (b) backlog from those customers burning off entirely during 2026, and (c) tiny prime-DoD obligation footprint visible in USAspending creates a structurally severe forward revenue gap. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY: forward pipeline depends on re-winning concentrated, unnamed federal customers whose remaining backlog completes within 12 months.

scores.claim_text: Total backlog ~$248M as of 12/31/2025; primary forward revenue anchor.
supports: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for BigBear.ai Federal / Pangiam contractor lookups — BBAI does not surface as a named PE prime in the J-Book corpus.

USAspending: $8.28M prime DoD obligations total. Even allowing for IDIQ ceilings and sub-tier work, the backlog/prime-obligation ratio (~30x) is much higher than typical defense primes, indicating either a heavy IDIQ ceiling component or sub-contracted work where prime contractors hold the ceiling.
Filing acknowledges backlog includes Priced Unexercised Options and that 'actual revenue may differ from backlog estimates' — material caveat.
scores.interpretation: Backlog is the headline forward indicator but not broken down by program/PE. Combined with tiny prime-DoD footprint, the $248M backlog is hard to triangulate independently. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: backlog is real per filing but the company has not provided J-Book-grounded line-item breakdown that would allow verification.

summary.framework_note: Pentagon J-Book corpus (410 PEs from FY26 RDT&E + Procurement) did not contain matches for any BBAI-disclosed program (Air Force EPASS, GFIM, Project Maven / Ask Sage / ConductorOS / biometric exit). The J-Book corpus is hardware-heavy (MDA, Space Force, Air Force aircraft); BBAI's exposure is to Army IT/services PEs and DHS (TSA/CBP) biometric programs which are outside corpus scope. This is a corpus coverage gap, not a J-Book divergence signal — heuristic 7 applied (NOT_FOUND => UNVERIFIABLE). The strongest signals came from the cross-check via USAspending: BigBear.ai Federal LLC has only $8.28M in prime DoD obligations (vs ~$128M FY25 revenue), the Army GFIM follow-on is a $3.9M production contract — small absolute scale relative to backlog and acquisition spend. Combined with the 51% revenue concentration burning off through 2026, the framework flags SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY on the customer-concentration/backlog claim (C5) without needing J-Book divergence.
